book_title: Six Revenue Engines — Inside Every Business Line
question: What does each Aurobindo business unit actually sell, who buys it, and how are revenue and profitability distributed across regions and modalities?

web_blocks.title: Segment Revenue Mix: FY25, FY26 & H1 FY27

web_blocks.html: Aurobindo reports sales across five commercial verticals: US Formulations, Europe Formulations, Growth Markets (RoW and India), Anti-Retrovirals (ARV), and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) [1, 3]. It also incubates two biologics units: CuraTeQ Biologics and TheraNym Biologics [1, 3]. Under Ind AS 108, the group reports one consolidated pharmaceutical segment without audited segment EBITDA margins [4]. Still, earnings call disclosures, gross margins, and subsidiary filings clarify the profit hierarchy [2, 7].

web_blocks.caption: Aurobindo Pharma: Verified Consolidated Revenue Mix Across Segments (FY25, FY26, Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27)
rows: US Formulations (incl. Eugia US, OTC & Lannett)
web_blocks.takeaway: Formulations generate 88% to 89% of revenue. Europe grew 23.4% in FY26 past €1 billion, while US sales jumped 25.2% YoY in Q2 FY27 post-Lannett [1, 2, 3]. (*FY25 includes ₹13 Cr Puerto Rico.)

web_blocks.title: 1. US Formulations (42.8% of FY26 Sales; 44.4% in Q2 FY27)

web_blocks.html: The US division remains Aurobindo's largest profit engine. Sales totaled ₹14,408 Cr in FY26, down 2.7% as transient gRevlimid revenue tapered [3]. Revenue then jumped 25.2% year-on-year to ₹4,555 Cr (USD 477 million) in Q2 FY27 [1]. As of September 30, 2026, Aurobindo held 900 US ANDA filings: 747 final approvals, 35 tentative approvals, and 118 under review [1]. Those filings address a USD 254.4 billion IQVIA market [1]. The portfolio spans oral solids (Unit III, Unit VII SEZ, APL HC IV), US controlled substances and inhalers (Lannett Seymour, Dayton, Raleigh), specialty dermatology (Acrotech), and sterile injectables via Eugia [1, 2, 13, 14].

Concrete US Example (Respiratory & Specialty Pivot): Consider an American asthma or COPD patient prescribed twice-daily fluticasone/salmeterol dry powder inhalation therapy. High device complexity long kept generic competition limited around GSK's Advair Diskus. On August 31, 2026, Aurobindo launched generic Advair (100/50 mcg and 250/50 mcg) through newly acquired Lannett, pairing inhaler device engineering with national wholesaler contracts [1, 2]. In October 2026, Acrotech launched ADQUEY (difamilast 1% ointment), an Otsuka-licensed PDE4 inhibitor NDA for atopic dermatitis backed by a dedicated US sales force [2, 14]. These launches layer higher-margin respiratory and branded drugs atop plain oral tablets.

Eugia Pharma Specialities Limited houses sterile injectables, oncology, hormones, and ophthalmics across Eugia Units I, II, III, SEZ, and Eugia Steriles [1, 3]. Its revenues sit inside the geographic segments above. Several years ago, Eugia leaned 70% toward the US and 30% toward the rest of the world [2]. By Q2 FY27, that mix balanced to 55% US and 45% RoW, heading toward 50:50 by FY28–FY29 [2]. In FY25, Eugia posted roughly ₹4,830 Cr (around USD 580 million) in subsidiary revenue, and CEO Yugandhar Puvvala confirmed ongoing double-digit dollar growth in Q2 FY27 [2].

Concrete Injectables Example: Consider a US hospital pharmacy stocking intravenous oncology and anti-infective vials for daily inpatient care. Hospital Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs) like Vizient and Premier award multi-year contracts based on sterility and supply reliability. Eugia produces lyophilized vials and pre-filled syringes across 239 specialty ANDAs—174 approved and 65 awaiting final approval [1]. Yet when Eugia Unit III (39 pending ANDAs) or Unit I (11 pending ANDAs) holds Official Action Indicated (OAI) status, current drugs keep shipping unless banned, while new ANDA approvals freeze until remediation closes [1, 8, 9].

web_blocks.title: 3. Europe Formulations (30.7% of FY26 Sales; 30.8% in Q2 FY27)

web_blocks.html: Europe is Aurobindo's steadiest growth engine. Revenue climbed 23.4% in FY26 to ₹10,315 Cr, crossing €1 billion annually [3, 6]. In Q2 FY27, Europe jumped 27.5% year-on-year to ₹3,161 Cr (€288 million; +18% in constant currency) [1, 2]. Operating across 10 countries—including the UK, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, and the Czech Republic—Aurobindo holds 4,344 European registrations [3, 6]. Dedicated Vizag Unit 15 and the 2-billion-dose Taizhou, China oral plant supply this network, with Taizhou now shipping 15+ products and reaching Q3 FY27 breakeven [2].

Concrete Europe Example: Walk into a pharmacy in Lisbon, Portugal, where Aurobindo subsidiary Generis is the market leader [2]. When a patient brings a prescription for a generic cardiovascular statin, Portuguese reimbursement rules favor pharmacy-level substitution. Aurobindo makes the API in Hyderabad, presses blister packs at Vizag Unit 15 or Taizhou under EU-GMP standards, and delivers overnight via Generis depots—capturing both factory margin and local brand loyalty.

web_blocks.title: 4. Growth Markets (10.4% of FY26 Sales) & India Branded Domestic

web_blocks.html: Growth Markets generated ₹3,499 Cr in FY26 (+10.0% YoY) and ₹1,026 Cr in Q2 FY27 (+16.3% YoY), led by Canada, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa, Colombia, Chile, and Southeast Asia [1, 3]. Domestic Indian sales were tiny at ₹76 Cr in Q4 FY26 [3]. To build Indian scale, Auropharm paid ₹300 Cr upfront in January 2026 for Khandelwal Laboratories' 23 non-oncology prescription brands in anti-infectives and pain care [4, 15]. In April 2026, Aurobindo consolidated all domestic branded generics into Auropharm Limited [4].

Concrete Growth Markets Example: In Canada, where Aurobindo holds 282 formulation filings, provincial formularies enforce strict reference pricing [3]. Local arm Auro Pharma Inc. sells oral cardiovascular tablets alongside newly approved CuraTeQ biosimilars such as Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim) and Bevqolva (bevacizumab) [3, 20]. Using existing pharmacy relationships lets Aurobindo launch biologics with low extra selling cost [3].

ARV sales grew 33.5% in FY26 to ₹1,384 Cr and reached ₹359 Cr (USD 38 million) in Q2 FY27 [1, 3]. While margins are modest, multi-year tender volumes keep large oral solid tablet lines running near full utilization.

Concrete ARV Example: Global agencies like PEPFAR and the Global Fund run sealed tenders for triple-combination HIV tablets such as tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir (TLD) across sub-Saharan Africa. Aurobindo holds 6 USFDA tentative approvals specifically for PEPFAR [1]. Producing both APIs and finished tablets internally lets it win billion-tablet annual allocations where fractions of a cent per dose decide winners.

web_blocks.title: 6. Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients / API (12.0% of FY26 Sales) & Pen-G

web_blocks.html: External API revenue totaled ₹4,047 Cr in FY26 (₹2,759 Cr Beta-lactams; ₹1,288 Cr Non Beta-lactams) and rose 20.9% YoY to ₹1,162 Cr in Q2 FY27 [1, 3]. Supported by 322 US Drug Master Files (DMFs) and 2,153 European filings, APIs also feed roughly half of Aurobindo's internal tablet volume [3]. At the heart sits Lyfius Pharma's 15,000 MTPA Pen-G fermentation plant in Kakinada, now producing ~10,000 MTPA annualized and operating EBITDA-positive before PLI incentives [2].

Concrete API Example: Amoxicillin—one of the world's most prescribed antibiotics—starts with Penicillin-G potassium fermented from corn steep liquor. Enzymes convert Pen-G into 6-APA, which is then synthesized into amoxicillin API. For decades, India imported nearly all Pen-G and 6-APA from China. Today, Aurobindo ferments Pen-G at Kakinada, converts it into 6-APA for internal Unit XII and domestic corporate buyers, and has petitioned India's trade authorities for anti-dumping protection against Chinese dumping [2, 7].

web_blocks.title: 7. Incubating Engines: CuraTeQ Biosimilars & TheraNym Biologics CMO

web_blocks.html: CuraTeQ Biologics has launched four oncology biosimilars across Europe, the UK, Canada, and India: Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim), Zefylti (filgrastim), Bevqolva (bevacizumab), and Dazublys (trastuzumab) [1, 3, 20]. Denosumab (Fugevy/Filvizy) and omalizumab (Omazijev) are filed with the EMA, with USFDA filings slated next [1]. A March 2026 STADA pact expands distribution in France and Germany [3]. Meanwhile, TheraNym Biologics is building 120 KL of mammalian bioreactors across Unit 1 (60 KL, qualifying March 2027) and Unit 2 (60 KL, USD 180 million capex, ready 2030) for anchor partner MSD, targeting CMO revenue from 2028 [1, 2].

book_paragraphs: From the outside, Aurobindo Pharma looks like one sprawling generic pill exporter. Once you open the segment breakdown, however, you find seven distinct engines running under very different customer rules, factory physics, and profit margins.

At the top sits the United States, generating ₹14,408 crore in FY26 and jumping 25.2 percent year-on-year to ₹4,555 crore in Q2 FY27. Never lump all American drug sales into one mental bucket. Think of Aurobindo USA in four distinct layers that balance each other.

Layer one holds high-volume oral tablets coming out of Telangana mega-plants like Unit VII SEZ. Those pills battle daily on price against rival generic makers. Layer two holds US-manufactured controlled substances and respiratory inhalers, boosted sharply by the June 2026 acquisition of Lannett and the August 2026 launch of generic Advair Diskus. Inhalers demand complex dry-powder engineering, keeping dozens of small tablet packagers out.

Layer three is branded US dermatology under Acrotech, highlighted by the October 2026 launch of eczema ointment ADQUEY. Unlike generic pills, ADQUEY requires a dedicated specialty sales team visiting dermatologists. Layer four is Eugia's sterile hospital injectables—vials and pre-filled syringes used in chemotherapy and critical care. Holding 900 US ANDA filings targeting a 254-billion-dollar IQVIA market gives Aurobindo huge shelf coverage at wholesalers, even when older molecules like gRevlimid roll off.

Look closely at Eugia within that mix, because its role is shifting fast. Years ago, Eugia relied 70 percent on the United States and 30 percent on international markets. After posting roughly ₹4,830 crore in FY25 revenue, Eugia kept growing double digits while balancing its footprint to 55 percent US and 45 percent rest-of-world, heading toward 50:50 by FY29. That geographic balance softens any single-country inspection shock.

Right beside America stands Europe, which quietly evolved into Aurobindo's steadiest growth engine. European sales climbed 23.4 percent in FY26 to ₹10,315 crore, passing one billion euros annually. In Q2 FY27 alone, Europe reached ₹3,161 crore, growing 18 percent in constant currency. Aurobindo runs local subsidiaries across ten countries and holds 4,344 European registrations.

Why does Europe behave so much calmer than America? Walk into a neighborhood pharmacy in Lisbon, where Aurobindo subsidiary Generis leads the local market. When a patient hands over a statin prescription, local reimbursement rules favor steady pharmacy brands backed by reliable overnight delivery. Because ten fragmented country markets never rebid overnight like three American buyer groups, Europe supplies predictable cash flow while Vizag Unit 15 and Taizhou, China ramp up.

Next come three smaller pillars that serve vital industrial roles: Growth Markets, Anti-Retrovirals, and external APIs. Growth Markets delivered ₹3,499 crore in FY26 across Canada, Brazil, South Africa, Mexico, Colombia, Chile, and Asia, rising 16.3 percent in Q2 FY27. In Canada alone, 282 filings let Aurobindo sell everyday oral pills alongside newly approved CuraTeQ biosimilars through the same local team. Meanwhile, to cure its historically tiny ₹76-crore quarterly domestic presence, Auropharm paid ₹300 crore upfront in January 2026 for 23 prescription brands from Khandelwal Labs.

Anti-Retrovirals generated ₹1,384 crore in FY26, jumping 33.5 percent as PEPFAR and Global Fund tenders ordered billion-tablet lots of triple-combination TLD HIV medicine for Africa. Margins per pill are razor-thin, yet huge steady runs keep Aurobindo's massive oral lines humming near full utilization. External APIs added ₹4,047 crore in FY26 across beta-lactam antibiotics and non-beta-lactam chemicals, backed by 322 US Drug Master Files and 2,153 European filings, while also feeding roughly half of Aurobindo's internal tablet volume.

Inside APIs sits one game-shifting industrial asset: Lyfius Pharma's 15,000-tonne Penicillin-G fermentation complex in Kakinada. Walk through the chemistry of Amoxicillin, one of the world's most common antibiotics. Factories ferment corn steep liquor into Penicillin-G, convert Pen-G with enzymes into 6-APA, and synthesize Amoxicillin API. For decades, India imported nearly every gram of Pen-G and 6-APA from China. By mid-FY27, Kakinada hit roughly 10,000 tonnes annualized output and turned EBITDA-positive even before counting PLI incentives—shielding Aurobindo's antibiotic plants while petitioning for anti-dumping duties against Chinese imports.

book_callouts.title: Why Geography Changes Generic Economics
book_callouts.quote: A tablet sold to a US wholesaler behaves like a futures contract; the same tablet sold to a Portuguese pharmacy behaves like a staple.
book_callouts.text: In America, three mega-buying groups rebid generic contracts every quarter with one click. In Western Europe, local brand trust, pharmacy substitution rules, and fragmented country tenders cushion violent price drops.

book_callouts.title: Why Pen-G Changes the Antibiotic Chain
book_callouts.quote: Owning fermentation turns a vulnerable buyer into the domestic price setter.
book_callouts.text: By making 10,000 tonnes of Pen-G a year in Kakinada and converting it into 6-APA and Amoxicillin, Aurobindo captures margin at three steps instead of paying Chinese suppliers.

book_subsections.title: Incubating Biologics & Concrete Hospital Mechanics
paragraphs: Above today's cash engines sit two multi-year growth options that are only beginning to move the income statement: CuraTeQ Biologics and TheraNym Biologics. Under Ind AS 108, Aurobindo folds everything into one reportable pharma segment, so investors must track these incubating bets through R&D disclosures and regulatory filings. CuraTeQ already markets four approved oncology biosimilars—Dyrupeg, Zefylti, Bevqolva, and Dazublys—across Europe, the UK, Canada, and India, bolstered by a March 2026 STADA alliance in France and Germany.

Next in line sit Denosumab and Omalizumab, both already filed with European regulators while USFDA filings queue up behind them. Behind CuraTeQ sits TheraNym Biologics, building 120 kiloliters of mammalian cell-culture capacity across two 60-kiloliter facilities anchored by global leader MSD. Unit 1 enters qualification around March 2027, Unit 2 breaks ground in October 2026 with 180 million dollars in planned capex for 2030, and commercial biologics contract revenue should begin stockpiling around 2028.

Also inspect the filing math behind this seven-part machine so you see why the product hopper stays full. As of September 30, 2026, Aurobindo held 900 US ANDAs targeting a 254.4-billion-dollar IQVIA market: 747 final approvals, 35 tentative approvals, and 118 applications still under FDA review. Across Eugia specifically, 239 specialty ANDAs cover 174 approved filings and 65 under review. Globally, the regulatory vault held 4,344 European registrations, 282 Canadian filings, and 4,436 API dossiers as of March 2026.

Step back and trace how all seven pieces connect in real hospitals and pharmacies. Picture an Ohio hospital pharmacist ordering sterile chemotherapy vials from Eugia, an American asthma patient refilling generic Advair made with Lannett's powder-inhaler engineering, and a Lisbon pharmacy stocking Generis statins. Picture a Canadian clinic switching onto CuraTeQ's pegfilgrastim biosimilar Dyrupeg, and an Indian clinic prescribing Khandelwal anti-infectives via Auropharm. Watch what happens to gross margins when that complex mix scales: in Q2 FY27, consolidated gross margin climbed 149 basis points year-on-year to 61.2 percent, proving that product breadth protects unit economics.

That geographic balance also softens dependence on any single buyer or currency. US formulations represent roughly 43 percent of FY26 sales, Europe contributes nearly 31 percent, Growth Markets and ARVs supply over 14 percent combined, and external APIs add 12 percent. Even when American wholesale tablet pricing fluctuates, steady European pharmacy demand and rising Kakinada Pen-G tonnage cushion consolidated operating profits.

One final point matters when reading Aurobindo's segment story. Total formulations already deliver 88 to 89 percent of group revenue, while external APIs contribute 11 to 12 percent. Inside APIs, Beta-lactams grew 24.8 percent year-on-year in Q2 FY27 to ₹858 crore while Non Beta-lactams reached ₹304 crore. That steady chemical base acts both as a third-party revenue line and as internal cost insurance for Aurobindo's tablet factories worldwide.

callouts.title: Check the Mix
callouts.quote: Follow where the gross margin expands, not just where the revenue headline grows.
callouts.text: Every point of gross margin improvement across ₹36,913 crore of trailing sales drops nearly ₹370 crore toward operating profit—provided overheads and sterile remediation do not eat it up.
